thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: multiple GPU nodes reporting Xid errors + ECC corrections. 6 nodes in prod-west showing driver resets -> container restarts. Severity: P1. Paging on-call now. <https://infra.redwood/status/incident/1752001234>
Ava L.: acked. I'm on it. paging Marcus and ops-hardware. working to get scope.
Marcus K.: looking. nvidia-smi shows Tainted driver resets on gpu0/gpu1 on node-gpu-07. dmesg has repeated 'Xid 31' and 'Xid 13' entries. suspect GPU hw/driver instability.
Priya S.: are we seeing OOMs in pods, or just driver resets?
Dan M.: containers are restarting, kube shows OOMKilled on some pods and CrashLoopBackOff on model-runtime for short bursts. Several requests got 502/503s last 10m. Customers: a handful of hosted customers hitting increased latency and errors.
eng-oncall: quick note: we have auto-fallback to smaller quantized model in routing policy for tier-basic — that should've kicked in for some routes. Is fallback working?
Marcus K.: fallback triggered for ~12% of requests. But routing still sent some to affected nodes before drain. We'll isolate nodes and force reroute.
SRE-Bot: detection rule: GPU ECC corrected errors > 100/min on node-gpu-07 -> escalated. Annotated logs: /var/log/gpu/ecc-1752001234.log
Ava L.: mitigation plan: 1) cordon node-gpu-{07,09,12} 2) drain safe with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data 3) restart nvidia-driver on node 07 4) if resets persist, reboot node and mark for hardware ticket 5) reroute traffic and scale up healthy pool. Doing step 1 now.
Priya S.: please capture nvidia-smi -q -d ECC and paste. also get dmesg snippet with Xid.
Marcus K.: paste: ```
$ nvidia-smi -q -d ECC
GPU 0000:01:00.0
    ECC Mode
        Current                    : On
        Pending                    : Off
    ECC Errors
        Volatile
            Single Bit
                Device Memory   : 125
                Register File   : 0
            Double Bit
                Device Memory   : 2
                Register File   : 0
```  
and dmesg: ```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (0001:0013): GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679234] NVRM: Xid (0001:0031): a GPU page fault was detected.
``` 
Marcus K.: also seeing 'GPU appears to be locked' messages and multiple driver resets in journalctl.
Dan M.: customer impact: support queue shows 9 tickets in last 20m, mainly high-throughput inference timeouts. Postgres event shows increased retry traffic.
support-bot: customer-impact: "short-lived 502/503s for inference API in prod-west, estimated affected requests ~0.4% over 10m". Sent notification to status page.
Ava L.: cordoned nodes: node-gpu-07, node-gpu-09, node-gpu-12. Starting drain on node-gpu-07 (graceful with 120s). Will watch for stuck pods.
Priya S.: while draining, please snapshot /sys/class/drm/card*/status and GPU power/temperature. could be thermal.
Marcus K.: captured temp/power: GPU0 temp=82C, power=285W. Not great. Thermal throttling seen.
ops-hardware: we need serial console logs; opening ticket with vendor. Please set 'quiesce' to avoid power spikes during reboot.
Ava L.: restart nvidia driver on node-gpu-07 now: `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-drm.service && sudo pkill -f nvidia` — will tail dmesg.
SRE-Bot: driver restart in progress on node-gpu-07. Watch for Xid recurrence.
Marcus K.: after driver restart a couple of new Xid 31 came through, containers still restarting. Going to reboot node.
Dan M.: rerouting traffic: increase capacity in prod-east by spinning up 4 extra inference workers and updating routing weights to prefer prod-east until we stabilize.
Priya S.: thanks. please add a temporary routing rule to avoid nodes with label gpu_faulty=true.
eng-oncall: enacted: added label and updated service weights. Traffic to faulty nodes dropped to <0.1%.
Ava L.: node-gpu-07 rebooted. Post-reboot ECC shows single-bit errors cleared but double-bit persists on one bank. Marking node for hardware replacement.
ops-hardware: confirmed. scheduling hardware swap for node-gpu-07; vendor ticket #HW-88421 opened. ETA on RMA: 48-72h. Marked for off-rotation.
Marcus K.: kept node-gpu-09/12 cordoned; monitoring for similar symptoms. node-gpu-09 shows rising ECC corrected counts but no Xid yet.
Dan M.: a few customers still saw degraded latency while routing shifted; status page updated with "Degraded performance — mitigation in progress". No data exfiltration.
Ava L.: postmortem actions (short list): 1) add automatic node isolation on repeated Xid 13/31 events 2) add thermal alarms at 75C sustained 3) revise routing to preemptively reduce load on nodes with rising ECC counts 4) infra runbook update for driver restart -> reboot -> RMA
Priya S.: also add nightly ECC scan metric and alert if corrected errors per minute > 10.
Marcus K.: adding temporary engine-level throttle to reduce power draw for older GPUs while we rotate replacements.
SRE-Bot: incident severity downgraded to P2; continued monitoring for 6h. Capture: slack thread archived to incident ticket.
Ava L.: handing off to Marcus for next 8h watch. Summary for handoff: 3 nodes affected, hardware RMA opened for node-gpu-07, routing healthy, customers seeing transient 502s earlier but now reduced. See vendor ticket HW-88421 and logs at /var/log/gpu/ecc-1752001234.log
Marcus K.: ack. I'll take watch. Will escalate to Priya if new Xid spikes > 50/min or double-bit ECC > 0.
support-bot: notified customers of mitigation and informed support queue. we'll follow up once hardware replaced.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity P2. node-gpu-07 out for RMA. Routing rerouted. Next update due in 2h or on status change.
Ava L.: thanks team. :thumbsup:
Marcus K.: lunchtime for me but staying on watch. ping if anything spikes.
Priya S.: thx, leaving notes in ticket"
